html:
The Declaration of Independence is the document in which thirteen British colonies in North America announced that they were free and independent states. The Second Continental Congress adopted it in Philadelphia on 4 July 1776.

The war with Britain had already been going on for over a year, since the fighting at Lexington and Concord in April 1775. Congress named a committee of five, including John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson, to draft a statement. Jefferson wrote most of it, and Congress then cut and changed it, removing a passage that blamed the king for the slave trade. Congress voted for independence on 2 July and approved the final text two days later.

The Declaration has three parts:

  • a short statement of political ideas, drawing on John Locke, that all men are created equal, with rights to "life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness", and that governments rest on the consent of the governed;
  • a long list of charges against King George III;
  • the formal declaration that the colonies were now free states.

Its words outlived its time. Many of the men who signed it owned slaves, and the gap between "all men are created equal" and slavery was pointed out at once. Later, Frederick Douglass, Abraham Lincoln and Martin Luther King Jr. all used it to argue for equality. It also became a model for independence declarations around the world, starting in Spanish America and Haiti. 4 July is the national day of the United States.
sum: The Declaration of Independence is the document in which thirteen British colonies in North America announced that they were free and independent states. The Second Continental Congress adopted it in Philadelphia on 4 July 1776.
